case: Batch concrete production and an enclosed shoreline station
observed: 256 and then 512 white concrete powder were crafted with exact whole-batch input/output balances.
The first open-shore run recovered 47 from 48 processed powder; missing material was not credited. Later production was paused near a hostile while health stayed 20.
A waterlogged oak leaf and a small cobblestone enclosure were built using ordinary client interactions; interior light and an owned removable roof hatch were verified.

Dry block approach refuses a fluid-containing anchor, including a full waterlogged leaf, with the misleading message Work block state changed. The placement adapter now chooses a dry supporting block instead.
Cruise arrival can leave lateral momentum. Precision placement uses the bounded route and confirmed grounded footing before interacting.

The observed route stalled on a 0.00510634 vertical residual before any horizontal motion. Runtime 1.7.65 accepts a 2.5 cm vertical settling band while retaining millimeter horizontal alignment and all host collision checks.

A pilot converted and recovered 8 concrete inside the enclosure at 20 health. Its older exit routine tried to rise from the pickup pit under a closed adjacent roof; Kit disconnected for a ceiling stall after 30 seconds, still at 20 health. Native and script health locks remained inactive; reconnection was then authorized under the user rule.
The corrected exit first returns to the dry stand and then rises through the owned hatch; this was live-verified at full health after reconnect.

Carried quantities are re-read before resuming. The next run started with 335 powder and 9 concrete, whose sum matched the earlier 344 material balance, rather than replaying a stale 336-item expectation.
remaining: The Starship is not finished. Material production is ongoing; this case does not prove the entire build, long-term immunity from death, or automatic reconnection after a health exit.
